newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean blue chips end lower on downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Chilean blue chips end lower on downgrades.

text.p: Although Chilean shares recouped some early losses in afternoon trade, the market closed at its lowest level in seven months on a series of downgrades from foreign brokerages, said traders.
The late rebound is seen following through Tuesday with stocks seen angling higher at the opening, they said.
"The market will be recovering lost ground, although with some measure of instability," said Lance Eckel, an analyst at brokerage Sud Americano.
The 40-share IPSA index ended off 0.63 percent at 94.68 points.
The general IGPA index closed down 0.57 percent at 5,172.66 points. Volume swelled to 14 billion pesos from 10 billion pesos Friday.
Rising world copper prices are seen helping copper stocks, especially mining firm Mantos Blancos which has just completed a major expansion, said dealers.
Mantos closed up 2.94 percent at 700 pesos. Copper products maker Madeco was changed at 960 pesos.
Traders said Lehman Brothers' decision to downgrade its Chilean position to underweight from overweight while increasing its Mexican weighting caught investors off guard.
"It came as a surprise as Lehman have been very bullish about Chile," said Eckel.
News of Kleinwort Benson's downgrading of its rating on fertilizer-maker Soquimich to sell from buy also depressed the market, they said.
The market was hurt by continuing speculation that the $450 million Genesis Chile Fund was liquidating part of its portfolio, although this was denied by officials.
"There is no truth in the rumor that we reducing the fund and much less that we are taking it back to England," said the fund's Chilean representative Christopher Brown.
Other winners included winery Concha y Toro, up 1.74 percent at 175 pesos and telecoms company Telex which rose 0.85 percent to 1,190 pesos.
Losers included fishing company Coloso, down 3.57 percent at 270 pesos and power utility Edelnor which shed 3.23 percent to 300 pesos.
